sources.provider: NASA / GSFC / Arizona State University (LROC Science Operations Center)
sources.product_name: LROC WAC South Pole Mosaic
sources.spatial_resolution: 400 m/pixel source; bundled copy is 1200×1200 px (≈507 m/pixel at the pole)
sources.coordinate_system: South polar stereographic; 0° meridian up, 90°E right (verified against named craters, 2026-11-14)
sources.verification: Bundled file; orientation re-verified by overlaying published crater coordinates (see docs/verification.md).
sources.notes: Imagery only — never an elevation source. Works offline; it is the fallback beneath every remote layer.

sources.provider: NASA Solar System Treks (JPL) — Moon Trek
sources.product_name: LRO LOLA shaded relief, south pole to 87.5°S
sources.spatial_resolution: 5 m/pixel product (from the identifier); WMTS levels 0–9, finest tiles 16.72 m/pixel
sources.coverage: Projected bounding box ±75 840 m about the pole (≈87.5°S–90°S)
sources.coordinate_system: Moon 2000 south polar stereographic (central meridian 0°, true scale at the pole, sphere R = 1 737 400 m) per the Trek API documentation for south-pole products; the layer's WMTS capabilities advertise the placeholder CRS urn:ogc:def:crs:EPSG::0
sources.attribution: NASA/JPL Solar System Treks; LRO LOLA
sources.verification: WMTS capabilities inspected 2026-11-14 (style, matrix set, levels, tile size, top-left corner, bounding box). Tile retrieval is done by the browser and could not be exercised from the build environment.
sources.notes: A hillshade RENDERING of elevation. It is imagery: CHANDRA never reads heights from it.

sources.provider: NASA Solar System Treks (JPL) — Moon Trek
sources.product_name: LROC WAC polar illumination percentage, south pole
sources.spatial_resolution: 100 m/pixel product (from the identifier); WMTS levels 0–6, finest tiles 133.78 m/pixel
sources.coverage: Projected bounding box x −60 884…61 116 m, y −61 187…61 213 m (≈88°S–90°S)
sources.coordinate_system: Moon 2000 south polar stereographic (central meridian 0°, true scale at the pole, sphere R = 1 737 400 m) per the Trek API documentation for south-pole products; the layer's WMTS capabilities advertise the placeholder CRS urn:ogc:def:crs:EPSG::0
sources.attribution: NASA/JPL Solar System Treks; LROC WAC
sources.verification: WMTS capabilities inspected 2026-11-14. Tile retrieval could not be exercised from the build environment.
sources.notes: A published illumination statistic shown as imagery. It is independent of CHANDRA's lighting computation and is not used by it.

sources.provider: LROC / Arizona State University (Lunaserv WMS)
sources.product_name: LROC WAC global mosaic (WMS layer luna_wac_global)
sources.coverage: Global layer; requested here only for the south-polar view
sources.coordinate_system: Requested as IAU2000:30120 (Moon south polar stereographic), which the service capabilities advertise
sources.verification: GetCapabilities inspected 2026-11-14 (webmap.lroc.asu.edu redirects to wms.im-ldi.com; formats and SRS list read). The layer name is documented by LROC and recognised by the server; a rendered image could not be confirmed from the build environment.
sources.notes: Server-rendered imagery. If the request fails the map says so and keeps the bundled basemap.

sources.provider: LROC / Arizona State University with Applied Coherent Technology
sources.product_name: Lunar QuickMap
sources.verification: No public API is documented. CHANDRA only builds a share-style link (extent + proj=10, the equirectangular view) and offers the coordinates for pasting; nothing is scraped.
sources.notes: Use QuickMap to explore NAC footprints, illumination and topographic products interactively. For polar sites switch QuickMap to its south-pole projection after opening.

sources.provider: NASA GSFC Planetary Geodesy Data Archive (PGDA)
sources.product_name: A New View of the Lunar South Pole from LOLA — LDEM_80S_20MPP_ADJ.TIF
sources.version: ADJ (adjusted LOLA mosaic; no version number stated on the product page)
sources.coordinate_system: South polar stereographic X/Y in metres; cloud-optimised GeoTIFF (stated on the product page). Projection parameters are read and validated from the file at acquisition time.
sources.reference_frame: MOON_ME, JPL DE421 (stated on the product page)
sources.vertical_datum: Surface height in metres (product page). CHANDRA applies a 1 737 400 m reference sphere from its acquisition configuration — confirm against the product documentation before mission use.
sources.attribution: NASA GSFC PGDA; author listed on the product page: Michael Kenneth Barker
sources.verification: Product page inspected 2026-11-14. Bounded HTTP range acquisition is implemented and tested against a local range server; live access from the build environment could not be verified.
sources.notes: Whole product is 2.6 GB; CHANDRA never downloads it — only the native-resolution window around a site. Default acquisition product.

sources.provider: NASA/JPL Solar System Dynamics
sources.product_name: Horizons on-line ephemeris system (API)
sources.version: API 1.2; planetary/lunar ephemeris DE441 (reported in responses)
sources.coverage: Sun (10) and Earth (399) as seen from a lunar surface site (coord@301)
sources.coordinate_system: Topocentric airless-apparent azimuth/elevation; site given as east longitude, latitude, altitude
sources.reference_frame: MEAN_ME lunar body-fixed frame, 1737.4 km sphere (reported in responses)
sources.attribution: NASA/JPL Solar System Dynamics Group, Horizons On-Line Ephemeris System
sources.verification: Live responses recorded 2026-11-14 are stored as test fixtures; every response is validated (bodies, site echo, frame, radii, refraction, timestamps) before use.
sources.notes: Independent verification source only. It never replaces CHANDRA's ephemeris engine and contains no terrain.
